newsitem.title: UK: Freelance reporter linked to British budget leak.
newsitem.headline: Freelance reporter linked to British budget leak.

text.p: A freelance journalist was believed to be the source of the leak of top secret documents about Britain's budget before it was officially announced, the Guardian reported on Wednesday.
The Guardian said the Daily Mirror tabloid obtained the documents from the journalist, who had a record for spectacular scoops. It did not name the journalist.
"Workers are to be questioned at a south London print plant...where many staff have been told they face redundancy, and where budget papers are normally printed," said the Guardian.
The Daily Mirror, which supports the opposition Labour Party, said it received the 36 documents late on Monday -- a day before finance minister Kenneth Clarke announced the budget in parliament.
The tabloid said Prime Minister John Major's office had confirmed that the documents, which totalled about 100 pages, were genuine.

The government obtained an injunction prohibiting the Daily Mirror from publishing the documents but the tabloid said it had already decided to hand them back to Clarke's office because a premature disclosure of the budget could have caused chaos on international stock markets.
Thirty-three of the documents were said to be from the Inland Revenue tax authorities, two from customs and excise and one from the office dealing with Scottish affairs.
A spokesman at the journalist's business address told the Guardian: "He is not in the office at the moment but we have been receiving lots of calls from people asking to speak to him."
Major's office confirmed on Tuesday that police had been called in to investigate the leak, which was highly embarrassing for the government.
In 1947, finance minister Hugh Dalton resigned after leaking parts of his budget to a reporter.
